One sentence: **a configured `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` becomes the actual patience of fa's run-idle watchdog — a warming-up model gets exactly the patience the user configured, not a hardcoded ~959s.**

Continuation of #1554: gh-1554 added `providerTimeouts.connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (and per-entry scoped overrides in the roles chain / customProviders, riding the model as request-scoped watchdog windows). But a separate mechanism — the **run-idle watchdog** ("agent stalled no response for 2m … /restart", zero-byte replay ×3) — kills a silent stream after ~959s regardless, so on models with a ~30-minute warmup (self-hosted llama.cpp) fa still aborts while the model "reasons into the void". User expectation: wait until the configured timeout.

## Why this framing
- The two mechanisms must compose, not compete: **watchdog patience = f(effective streamIdleTimeout)**, not an independent constant. Retracted framing: "remove the watchdog" — it protects against genuinely dead endpoints; it must keep firing on the default.
- The fix is precedence plumbing (gh-1554's request-scoped window already rides the model), not a new timeout system.

## Architecture
- Components: **run-idle watchdog** (TUI stall notice + zero-byte replay, lives around the provider stream in `fallback_stream` / `providers_queue_runtime` / `transient_retry_stream`), **providerTimeouts** (global `provider: connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs` + gh-1554 per-entry overrides), **transient retry** path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1:** effective watchdog idle window = `max(2 min default, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective = gh-1554 precedence (entry override > global > default).
  - **I2:** replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ `connectTimeoutMs` when set (no infinite replay loop); each replay is logged with which window governed it.
  - **I3:** unset config ⇒ today's behavior byte-for-byte (2m notice, 3 replays, ~959s abort) — no regression for default users.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stall notice threshold | fixed 2m | derived from I1 (notice text names the governing value and its source: global / entry override / default) |
| Zero-byte replay | ×3 fixed | attempts bounded by remaining `connectTimeoutMs` budget (I2); replay event carries `idleWindowMs` |
| Per-entry override | gh-1554 rides the model to the provider | **also read by the run-idle watchdog** (the actual gap) |
| Terminal error | `(zero-byte stall)` after 959s | names window + attempts + source; suggests raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` |
| Warmup-aware UX (progress ping) | — | excluded: server-side keep-alive is llama.cpp's job, not fa's |

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs: 2000000` (+ customProviders entry per #1617's config): a scripted provider that sends zero bytes for 35 min then responds → the run **survives**, the stall notice fires at the configured window, no `(zero-byte stall)` abort. Hook: IT with a fake slow provider (deterministic clock).
- **AC2** — per-entry override on a `customProviders`/roles-chain entry wins over the global for that entry only (gh-1554 semantics extend to the watchdog).
- **AC3** — unset config: default behavior identical to today (2m / 3 replays / abort) — existing tests green unchanged.
- **AC4** — replay bound: with `connectTimeoutMs` < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values.
- **AC5** — terminal error + stall notice name the effective window and its precedence source.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — precedence resolution: default < global < entry override (I1); replay budget math (AC4).
- `IT-*` — fake provider emitting silence for N minutes (deterministic clock): configured-window survival (AC1), entry-override win (AC2), default parity (AC3), budget stop (AC4).
- `E2E-1` — llama.cpp-shaped manual smoke: warming endpoint + 2M ms config completes a chat turn.

- No change to gh-1554's provider-level timeout mechanics; no new config keys; no keep-alive/ping spoofing; no changes to transient 429/5xx retry (#1602's sibling).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

One sentence: **a configured `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` becomes the actual patience of fa's run-idle watchdog — a warming-up model gets exactly the patience the user configured, not a hardcoded ~959s.**

Continuation of #1554: gh-1554 added `providerTimeouts.connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (and per-entry scoped overrides in the roles chain / customProviders, riding the model as request-scoped watchdog windows). User expectation: wait until the configured timeout.

## Why this framing
- The two mechanisms must compose, not compete: **watchdog patience = f(effective streamIdleTimeout)**, not an independent constant. Retracted framing: "remove the watchdog" — it protects against genuinely dead endpoints; it must keep firing on the default.
- The fix is precedence plumbing (gh-1554's request-scoped window already rides the model), not a new timeout system.

## Architecture
- Components: **run-idle watchdog** (TUI stall notice + zero-byte replay, lives around the provider stream in `fallback_stream` / `providers_queue_runtime` / `transient_retry_stream`), **providerTimeouts** (global `provider: connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs` + gh-1554 per-entry overrides), **transient retry** path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1:** effective watchdog idle window = `max(2 min default, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective = gh-1554 precedence (entry override > global > default).
  - **I2:** replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ `connectTimeoutMs` when set (no infinite replay loop); each replay is logged with which window governed it.
  - **I3:** unset config ⇒ today's behavior byte-for-byte (2m notice, 3 replays, ~959s abort) — no regression for default users.

| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stall notice threshold | fixed 2m | derived from I1 (notice text names the governing value and its source: global / entry override / default) |
| Zero-byte replay | ×3 fixed | attempts bounded by remaining `connectTimeoutMs` budget (I2); replay event carries `idleWindowMs` |
| Per-entry override | gh-1554 rides the model to the provider | **also read by the run-idle watchdog** (the actual gap) |
| Terminal error | `(zero-byte stall)` after 959s | names window + attempts + source; suggests raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` |
| Warmup-aware UX (progress ping) | — | excluded: server-side keep-alive is llama.cpp's job, not fa's |

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs: 2000000` (+ customProviders entry per #1617's config): a scripted provider that sends zero bytes for 35 min then responds → the run **survives**, the stall notice fires at the configured window, no `(zero-byte stall)` abort. Hook: IT with a fake slow provider (deterministic clock).
- **AC2** — per-entry override on a `customProviders`/roles-chain entry wins over the global for that entry only (gh-1554 semantics extend to the watchdog).
- **AC3** — unset config: default behavior identical to today (2m / 3 replays / abort) — existing tests green unchanged.
- **AC4** — replay bound: with `connectTimeoutMs` < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values.
- **AC5** — terminal error + stall notice name the effective window and its precedence source.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — precedence resolution: default < global < entry override (I1); replay budget math (AC4).
- `IT-*` — fake provider emitting silence for N minutes (deterministic clock): configured-window survival (AC1), entry-override win (AC2), default parity (AC3), budget stop (AC4).

- No change to gh-1554's provider-level timeout mechanics; no new config keys; no keep-alive/ping spoofing; no changes to transient 429/5xx retry (#1602's sibling).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195

    "description": "## Goal — provider-aware run-idle watchdog (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **a configured `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` becomes the actual patience of fa's run-idle watchdog — a warming-up model gets exactly the patience the user configured, not a hardcoded ~959s.**

Continuation of #1554: gh-1554 added `providerTimeouts.connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (and per-entry scoped overrides in the roles chain / customProviders, riding the model as request-scoped watchdog windows). But a separate mechanism — the **run-idle watchdog** ("agent stalled no response for 2m … /restart", zero-byte replay ×3) — kills a silent stream after ~959s regardless, so on models with a ~30-minute warmup (self-hosted llama.cpp) fa still aborts while the model "reasons into the void". User expectation: wait until the configured timeout.

## Why this framing
- The two mechanisms must compose, not compete: **watchdog patience = f(effective streamIdleTimeout)**, not an independent constant. Retracted framing: "remove the watchdog" — it protects against genuinely dead endpoints; it must keep firing on the default.
- The fix is precedence plumbing (gh-1554's request-scoped window already rides the model), not a new timeout system.

## Architecture
- Components: **run-idle watchdog** (TUI stall notice + zero-byte replay, lives around the provider stream in `fallback_stream` / `providers_queue_runtime` / `transient_retry_stream`), **providerTimeouts** (global `provider: connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs` + gh-1554 per-entry overrides), **transient retry** path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1:** effective watchdog idle window = `max(2 min default, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective = gh-1554 precedence (entry override > global > default).
  - **I2:** replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ `connectTimeoutMs` when set (no infinite replay loop); each replay is logged with which window governed it.
  - **I3:** unset config ⇒ today's behavior byte-for-byte (2m notice, 3 replays, ~959s abort) — no regression for default users.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stall notice threshold | fixed 2m | derived from I1 (notice text names the governing value and its source: global / entry override / default) |
| Zero-byte replay | ×3 fixed | attempts bounded by remaining `connectTimeoutMs` budget (I2); replay event carries `idleWindowMs` |
| Per-entry override | gh-1554 rides the model to the provider | **also read by the run-idle watchdog** (the actual gap) |
| Terminal error | `(zero-byte stall)` after 959s | names window + attempts + source; suggests raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` |
| Warmup-aware UX (progress ping) | — | excluded: server-side keep-alive is llama.cpp's job, not fa's |

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs: 2000000` (+ customProviders entry per #1617's config): a scripted provider that sends zero bytes for 35 min then responds → the run **survives**, the stall notice fires at the configured window, no `(zero-byte stall)` abort. Hook: IT with a fake slow provider (deterministic clock).
- **AC2** — per-entry override on a `customProviders`/roles-chain entry wins over the global for that entry only (gh-1554 semantics extend to the watchdog).
- **AC3** — unset config: default behavior identical to today (2m / 3 replays / abort) — existing tests green unchanged.
- **AC4** — replay bound: with `connectTimeoutMs` < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values.
- **AC5** — terminal error + stall notice name the effective window and its precedence source.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — precedence resolution: default < global < entry override (I1); replay budget math (AC4).
- `IT-*` — fake provider emitting silence for N minutes (deterministic clock): configured-window survival (AC1), entry-override win (AC2), default parity (AC3), budget stop (AC4).
- `E2E-1` — llama.cpp-shaped manual smoke: warming endpoint + 2M ms config completes a chat turn.
- `REG-1` — CI job runs the IT suite on every PR touching `providers/`, `model_roles/`, or the watchdog; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — replayed request may still complete server-side (duplicate reply / double billing): on replay, the first request is aborted via CancelToken and its partial stream is dropped; document that billing dedup is provider-side. **E2** — stream dies between replays: transient-retry path takes over unchanged. **E3** — timeout raised mid-session: applies to the next request (no live re-arm), documented.

## Non-goals
- No change to gh-1554's provider-level timeout mechanics; no new config keys; no keep-alive/ping spoofing; no changes to transient 429/5xx retry (#1602's sibling).

1. Should the stall **notice** stay at 2m for UX (early "still waiting" feedback) while the *kill* moves to the configured window? *Sketched default: yes — notice at min(2m, window), kill at window.*
2. Backport the same precedence to the connect-phase watchdog in the same card? *Default: yes, one mechanism, one fix.*

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives)",
    "description": "## Goal — provider-aware run-idle watchdog (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **a configured `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` becomes the actual patience of fa's run-idle watchdog — a warming-up model gets exactly the patience the user configured, not a hardcoded ~959s.**

Continuation of #1554: gh-1554 added `providerTimeouts.connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (and per-entry scoped overrides in the roles chain / customProviders, riding the model as request-scoped watchdog windows). But a separate mechanism — the **run-idle watchdog** ("agent stalled no response for 2m … /restart", zero-byte replay ×3) — kills a silent stream after ~959s regardless, so on models with a ~30-minute warmup (self-hosted llama.cpp) fa still aborts while the model "reasons into the void". User expectation: wait until the configured timeout.

## Why this framing
- The two mechanisms must compose, not compete: **watchdog patience = f(effective streamIdleTimeout)**, not an independent constant. Retracted framing: "remove the watchdog" — it protects against genuinely dead endpoints; it must keep firing on the default.
- The fix is precedence plumbing (gh-1554's request-scoped window already rides the model), not a new timeout system.

## Architecture
- Components: **run-idle watchdog** (TUI stall notice + zero-byte replay, lives around the provider stream in `fallback_stream` / `providers_queue_runtime` / `transient_retry_stream`), **providerTimeouts** (global `provider: connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs` + gh-1554 per-entry overrides), **transient retry** path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1:** effective watchdog idle window = `max(2 min default, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective = gh-1554 precedence (entry override > global > default).
  - **I2:** replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ `connectTimeoutMs` when set (no infinite replay loop); each replay is logged with which window governed it.
  - **I3:** unset config ⇒ today's behavior byte-for-byte (2m notice, 3 replays, ~959s abort) — no regression for default users.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stall notice threshold | fixed 2m | derived from I1 (notice text names the governing value and its source: global / entry override / default) |
| Zero-byte replay | ×3 fixed | attempts bounded by remaining `connectTimeoutMs` budget (I2); replay event carries `idleWindowMs` |
| Per-entry override | gh-1554 rides the model to the provider | **also read by the run-idle watchdog** (the actual gap) |
| Terminal error | `(zero-byte stall)` after 959s | names window + attempts + source; suggests raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs` |
| Warmup-aware UX (progress ping) | — | excluded: server-side keep-alive is llama.cpp's job, not fa's |

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs: 2000000` (+ customProviders entry per #1617's config): a scripted provider that sends zero bytes for 35 min then responds → the run **survives**, the stall notice fires at the configured window, no `(zero-byte stall)` abort. Hook: IT with a fake slow provider (deterministic clock).
- **AC2** — per-entry override on a `customProviders`/roles-chain entry wins over the global for that entry only (gh-1554 semantics extend to the watchdog).
- **AC3** — unset config: default behavior identical to today (2m / 3 replays / abort) — existing tests green unchanged.
- **AC4** — replay bound: with `connectTimeoutMs` < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values.
- **AC5** — terminal error + stall notice name the effective window and its precedence source.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — precedence resolution: default < global < entry override (I1); replay budget math (AC4).
- `IT-*` — fake provider emitting silence for N minutes (deterministic clock): configured-window survival (AC1), entry-override win (AC2), default parity (AC3), budget stop (AC4).
- `E2E-1` — llama.cpp-shaped manual smoke: warming endpoint + 2M ms config completes a chat turn.
- `REG-1` — CI job runs the IT suite on every PR touching `providers/`, `model_roles/`, or the watchdog; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — replayed request may still complete server-side (duplicate reply / double billing): on replay, the first request is aborted via CancelToken and its partial stream is dropped; document that billing dedup is provider-side. **E2** — stream dies between replays: transient-retry path takes over unchanged. **E3** — timeout raised mid-session: applies to the next request (no live re-arm), documented.

## Non-goals
- No change to gh-1554's provider-level timeout mechanics; no new config keys; no keep-alive/ping spoofing; no changes to transient 429/5xx retry (#1602's sibling).

## Open questions
1. Should the stall **notice** stay at 2m for UX (early "still waiting" feedback) while the *kill* moves to the configured window? *Sketched default: yes — notice at min(2m, window), kill at window.*
2. Backport the same precedence to the connect-phase watchdog in the same card? *Default: yes, one mechanism, one fix.*

## References
- #1617 (original report: khoser, Ubuntu 24.04.4, fa 1.0.575, llama.cpp warmup ~30 min, 959s abort), #1554 (providerTimeouts + scoped entries), settings_registry `providerTimeouts`/`retry` yamlKeys.

Expected: wait until the configured timeout. Actual: aborts after ~959s.
</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure

OK, `_matchesBaseUrl` handles a null-parse baseUrl gracefully. `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` — if baseUrl is an empty string, `Uri.tryParse('')` returns an empty Uri (not null), then `matchesForUrl` won't match anything with scheme+authority, and resolution falls to global. Fine.

Now the key question: does `explicitStreamIdleForModel` correctly reproduce the precedence used at request time? At request time, the provider stream uses `providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl(url)` — which folds `effectiveProviderStreamIdleTimeout` = `providerTimeoutsOverride?.streamIdle ?? providerStreamIdleTimeout`. And registry entries take priority over global.

`resolveProviderTimeouts(url: url)` computes:
- chain: registry entries matching URL (no name — the call passes only url)
- field resolution: first entry declaring field → global → built-in default.

`explicitStreamIdleForModel` uses `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: url)` and rejects `builtIn` source. So:
- scoped model.streamIdleTimeout (roles chain entry) wins — matches gh-1554 semantics since the model carries the request-scoped override.
- then registry matches for URL.
- then global (globalOverride source, label 'global').
- built-in → null (keeps run watchdog floor).

Wait — but there's one subtlety: `model.streamIdleTimeout` — where does that get set? In the roles chain, entry overrides ride the model. If BOTH scoped and registry entries exist, scoped wins — consistent.

Another subtlety: `resolveProviderTimeouts` also accepts `name` param for explicit-name lookups — not passed here. That's OK — matches `providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl`.

But wait: is there an inconsistency with env fold-in? `providerTimeoutsOverride` is "the global `providerTimeouts:` section (or env fold-in)". So globalOverride covers env too. Good.

Let me look at agent.dart around the watchdog arm points, and how `_state.model` relates to the failover. This is a per-event cost that used to be just `Timer(...)`. `Uri.tryParse` of a URL is cheap but non-trivial; the registry scan is a list walk with sorts... Then `_armRunWatchdog` cancels a timer and creates a new Timer — that was already happening per event before. The added cost is 2 URI parses + 2 registry scans per event. Probably fine (microseconds), but doubling `runIdleWindow` calls is trivially avoidable:

_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);

Both invocations happen synchronously in sequence so results are consistent (registry is mutable mid-run in theory — `providerTuningRegistry` is "read on every request, seeded at boot, tests may set it directly" — a concurrent mutation between the two getter calls would produce mismatched window/info. But it's synchronous Dart code, single-threaded — no await between, so no mutation can happen between. Fine.)

OK, `_matchesBaseUrl` handles a null-parse baseUrl gracefully. `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` — if baseUrl is an empty string, `Uri.tryParse('')` returns an empty Uri (not null), then `matchesForUrl` won't match anything with scheme+authority, and resolution falls to global. Fine.

Now the key question: does `explicitStreamIdleForModel` correctly reproduce the precedence used at request time? At request time, the provider stream uses `providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl(url)` — which folds `effectiveProviderStreamIdleTimeout` = `providerTimeoutsOverride?.streamIdle ?? providerStreamIdleTimeout`. And registry entries take priority over global.

`resolveProviderTimeouts(url: url)` computes:
- chain: registry entries matching URL (no name — the call passes only url)
- field resolution: first entry declaring field → global → built-in default.

`explicitStreamIdleForModel` uses `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: url)` and rejects `builtIn` source. So:
- scoped model.streamIdleTimeout (roles chain entry) wins — matches gh-1554 semantics since the model carries the request-scoped override.
- then registry matches for URL.
- then global (globalOverride source, label 'global').
- built-in → null (keeps run watchdog floor).

Wait — but there's one subtlety: `model.streamIdleTimeout` — where does that get set? In the roles chain, entry overrides ride the model. If BOTH scoped and registry entries exist, scoped wins — consistent.

Another subtlety: `resolveProviderTimeouts` also accepts `name` param for explicit-name lookups — not passed here. That's OK — matches `providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl`.

But wait: is there an inconsistency with env fold-in? `providerTimeoutsOverride` is "the global `providerTimeouts:` section (or env fold-in)". So globalOverride covers env too. Good.

Now, important logic check: `zeroByteAttemptBudget` with `windowStory.window`.

`_zeroByteWindowStory(model, watchdogWindow)`:
- `fireWindow` = the watchdog fire's duration (the derived agent window) — the interval that governed the kill.
- else `explicit?.$1` (model's explicit idle)
- else `providerStreamIdleTimeout` (the built-in 5 min default).

Budget = `1 + connectBudget ~/ window` clamped to [1, ladderBound=2].

Consider the actual user scenario from the ticket: config `connectTimeoutMs: 20000, streamIdleTimeoutMs: 20000`. Window = 2000s (33 min). Budget = 1 + 20000/20000 = 2. Clamped to 2. So 2 attempts allowed: attempt 1 killed at 2000s, replay, attempt 2 killed at 2000s → total 4000s silent > connectTimeout 2000s. Hmm — the ticket AC4 says "replay bound: with connectTimeoutMs < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values." And I2: "replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs when set (no infinite replay loop)".

With budget = 1 + budget~/window: 2 attempts = 2 × window of silence = 2×window total silent patience, but connectBudget = window → total patience = 2×window > connectBudget. So I2's invariant "total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs" is violated? Let's think again. Actually the invariant as stated in the ticket is I2: "total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs when set (no infinite replay loop)". The formula 1 + budget ~/ window gives: budget=window → 2 attempts → 2 windows of silence, exceeding the budget. Now I understand the agent-side change. Key observations:

1. `_armRunWatchdog` now calls `runIdleWindow` TWICE (once for `window`, once for `_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow`) — a minor inefficiency: `runIdleWindow` getter is invoked twice, each doing `explicitStreamIdleForModel(_state.model)` which parses the URI and resolves the registry. It's not a hot path (arm happens per event batch — actually `_touchRunWatchdog` runs on EVERY agent event!). Wait — `_processEvent` calls `_touchRunWatchdog(event)` on every event, which calls `_armRunWatchdog()` on every non-tool event. And now `_armRunWatchdog` calls `runIdleWindow` twice → 2x `Uri.tryParse` + registry scan per event. Message streaming events (MessageUpdateEvent) can arrive frequently (per SSE chunk). This is a per-event cost that used to be just `Timer(...)`. `Uri.tryParse` of a URL is cheap but non-trivial; the registry scan is a list walk with sorts... Actually `matchesForUrl` builds a list, sorts it. On every streamed event (could be dozens per second), 2x. This is probably acceptable perf-wise but is a real change in hot-path cost. Hmm, worth flagging as SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Let me think — MessageUpdateEvent frequency: per SSE delta chunk, could be tens per second. Each arm: `runIdleWindow` getter called twice, each: `explicitStreamIdleForModel` → `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` (cheap), `resolveProviderTimeouts` → `forName` not called (name null), `matchesForUrl` → iterates registry entries, builds tuple list, sorts (n log n where n = registry size, typically small — a handful). Then `_armRunWatchdog` cancels a timer and creates a new Timer — that was already happening per event before. The added cost is 2 URI parses + 2 registry scans per event. Probably fine (microseconds), but doubling `runIdleWindow` calls is trivially avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

That's a SUGGESTION-level nit (perf, not correctness).

Actually wait — is it a real concern that `Timer` is re-created per event? That predates this PR. OK.

2. `_armedRunIdleInfo` initial value: `defaultRunIdleTimeout` — but if `runIdleTimeout` is customized by the host (constructor param), and the watchdog fires... wait, can `_onRunWatchdogFired` fire without `_armRunWatchdog` having run? The timer is only created in `_armRunWatchdog`, which sets `_armedRunIdleInfo`. So by the time `_onRunWatchdogFired` runs, `_armedRunIdleInfo` was set at arm time. The initial value only matters if... never, actually. OK.

But there's a subtle bug-ish thing: `_armedRunIdleInfo.raised` is computed as `window > runIdleTimeout`. And `_armRunWatchdog` captures `window = runIdleWindow.window` then re-invokes the getter for the record. Both invocations happen synchronously in sequence so results are consistent (registry is mutable mid-run in theory — `providerTuningRegistry` is "read on every request, seeded at boot, tests may set it directly" — a concurrent mutation between the two getter calls would produce mismatched window/info. But it's synchronous Dart code, single-threaded — no await between, so no mutation can happen between. Fine.)

3. `_onRunWatchdogFired`: after cancel, re-arms via `_armRunWatchdog()` — the re-arm re-derives the window. That matches "re-derives on every arm".

- else `providerStreamIdleTimeout` (the built-in 5 min default).

Budget = `1 + connectBudget ~/ window` clamped to [1, ladderBound=2].

Consider the actual user scenario from the ticket: config `connectTimeoutMs: 20000, streamIdleTimeoutMs: 20000`. Window = 2000s (33 min). Budget = 1 + 20000/20000 = 2. Clamped to 2. So 2 attempts allowed: attempt 1 killed at 2000s, replay, attempt 2 killed at 2000s → total 4000s silent > connectTimeout 2000s. Hmm — the ticket AC4 says "replay bound: with connectTimeoutMs < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget and errors naming both values." And I2: "replay attempts stay bounded: total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs when set (no infinite replay loop)".

With budget = 1 + budget~/window: 2 attempts = 2 × window of silence = 2×window total silent patience, but connectBudget = window → total patience = 2×window > connectBudget. So I2's invariant "total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs" is violated? Let's think again. Actually the invariant as stated in the ticket is I2: "total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs when set (no infinite replay loop)". The formula 1 + budget ~/ window gives: budget=window → 2 attempts → 2 windows of silence, exceeding the budget. Hmm, but "1 +" acknowledges the first attempt is the original request, and the budget buys replays: budget/window replays. First attempt (window) + floor(budget/window) replays... that's 1 + budget/window total windows = 2 windows with budget=window. So the formula's intent: "a budget at or above the window keeps the full bound (AC1's replay survives its own budget)". So they deliberately allow 2 windows of silence with a budget = 1 window. That's a deliberate trade-off documented in the dartdoc: "a budget at or above the window keeps the full bound". The I2 invariant in the ticket is about boundedness (no infinite loop), not a strict ≤ bound. The doc says "clamped into [1, ladderBound]... keeps the bound anti-infinite-loop guarantee in both directions". So it's documented as intentional. Borderline — the ticket's I2 literally says "total silent patience ≤ connectTimeoutMs when set", and the implementation gives up to 2×connectBudget. But the dartdoc redefines it. Is this a review finding? It's a design decision deviation from the ticket's literal invariant. Hmm. AC4 says "with connectTimeoutMs < Σ(replays), the watchdog stops at the connect budget". Σ(replays) — with window=2000s and 2 replays = 4000s... The original user config had BOTH connect and idle at 20000. With the implementation: budget=2, so first attempt 2000s killed, replay, second attempt 2000s killed → terminal. Total 4000s > 2000s budget. The user's expectation from the ticket: wait until the configured timeout (2000s warmup) — AC1: a provider silent 35 min then responds survives. 35 min = 2100s > 2000s window → first attempt killed at 2000s, then replay 2000s more → would the run survive? Each attempt can be silent for up to `window` before the watchdog kills it. So total silent patience ≤ attempts × window = (1 + budget~/window) × window ≈ window + budget. So total ≈ connectBudget + window ≤ 2 × connectBudget (when budget ≥ window). Strictly > connectBudget whenever ≥1 replay happens. So yes, the implementation deviates from the literal I2, but it's a deliberate documented decision ("AC1's replay survives its own budget") — because a strict ≤ bound would mean with budget == window, the first kill at window already exhausts the budget → no replay → AC1 would fail (35-min warmup killed at 33 min, never replayed... wait, would the warmup survive? attempt killed at 2000s, budget exhausted → terminal → run does NOT survive → AC1 violated). tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
